title: Understanding AI in the firm
purpose: Build on existing chatbot use to distinguish a fluent answer from a supported professional conclusion, then choose one firm task worth improving.
tool: Claude web in a new chat; Word or a text editor for the diagnostic and source. I operate the computer.

03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/01 Matter and Sources/Agreement - Executed v2.txt
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/01 Matter and Sources/Client Instruction.txt
04 Facilitator Materials/Teaching Resources/Entry and Exit Diagnostic.csv
04 Facilitator Materials/Teaching Resources/Diagnostic Answer Key.txt
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/05 Firm Adoption/In-Class Progress Record.csv
prepare: I open the seven entry questions and keep the answer key off the shared screen. I create a working copy of the progress record in the session output folder.
I open the executed agreement beside the chat and find the Key Terms adaptation replacing Section 12.6. I can point to the complete five-sentence passage.
steps: At slides 1–2, I ask the learner to describe one useful AI task and one frustrating result from current use, without client details. I use the seven entry questions as short reasoning checks, record the answers and avoid reteaching sound explanations. The existing diagnostic block stays within 15 minutes.
At the worked demonstration, I introduce Victoria as Customer and Equator as Provider. I say that ownership, assignment, change of control and continued responsibility are unconfirmed.
I start a new Claude chat, attach Agreement - Executed v2.txt and Client Instruction.txt, and confirm both filenames are visible. I paste S01-P1 and submit it once.
While it responds, I ask the learner to predict what facts are missing. I do not ask for confidential examples from a live client matter.
I put the answer beside KT-1. I underline the assignment trigger, change-of-control trigger and both exception conditions. I mark each factual statement supported, missing or invented.
If the answer is sound, I keep it as a successful observation. If it assumes consent from the label internal reorganisation, I hold the conclusion and request the missing transaction evidence.

During guided work, I compare four candidate tasks: total invoices, classify a document, find a precedent and draft an amendment. For each we choose a mechanism, identify where a chatbot alone is insufficient and name the evidence and review needed. I move quickly through familiar labels and spend the time on the design choice.
I choose one candidate task with the learner, name a proposed evidence owner and write one observable success test. I complete the progress record together in class.

prompts.text: Use only the attached fictional executed agreement and client instruction. Victoria asks whether its consent is required for Equator’s proposed internal reorganisation. Identify assignment and change-of-control obligations separately. Do not assume either trigger or the group-exception facts. Quote the controlling Key Terms passage and identify its location. Separate established facts, unresolved facts and a conditional conclusion. Identify the evidence Victoria should request. Keep this a short draft for human review; take no external action.

check: The controlling source is the Key Terms replacement, rather than the unmodified Standard Terms alone.
The base case remains unresolved because the transaction triggers and exception conditions have not been established. A confident yes/no without those facts fails the check.
The task map uses different mechanisms. A fixed known deadline needs a maintained date and reminder rule; it does not require training a model.
discuss: Does a genuine quotation make the conclusion correct?
No. The conclusion must follow from the quoted rule and established facts.
Who would own the source and review for the proposed task?
A proposed firm role is sufficient today; the class does not appoint a real owner without agreement.
rescue: Upload fails
I use the attachment route in the common setup, or paste the complete clearly labelled fictional source. If neither works within two minutes, I show the saved consent run and state its date.
The learner gives only terminology
I ask for one concrete task and what an acceptable output would contain.
record: The seven starting reasons, source/version, exact prompt and response, one checked conclusion, proposed task, owner and success test. I use a working copy, leaving the blank template intact.
transition: I say: Next we will look at what learning changes inside a model and what happens when it is used on a new document.
entry_question: Which part of a fluent consent answer would you sign off, and what evidence would you still request?
entry_focus: We compare the actual answer with the complete Key Terms and unresolved transaction facts. I ask for the release decision before discussing terminology.
executive_task: Choose one familiar firm task and decide whether a chat, a maintained retrieval workflow or ordinary software is sufficient. Name the evidence and reviewer required before a result is used.
executive_check: A defensible choice links the mechanism to the task and names a source owner, a success test and a hold condition. More AI is not automatically a better design.

title: How AI learns and represents information
purpose: Show the difference between training and inference, identifiers and learned representations, and similarity and legal meaning.
tool: PowerPoint diagrams, six paper/text document labels and the cached neural embedding self-test in Terminal.
files: 03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/02 Data and Retrieval/Language Representation Exercise.txt
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/02 Data and Retrieval/Learning and Embedding Examples.txt
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/02 Data and Retrieval/Concept Transfer Checks.txt
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/02 Data and Retrieval/embedding_selftest.py
prepare: I run s02_vectors before class and open Embedding Selftest.txt. I keep the actual measured cosine values, not a remembered number.

I put six labels on paper or in a text editor: signed service agreement; employee terms; credit note; sales invoice; privacy notice; board approval. The two-dimensional slide map is explicitly illustrative.
steps: I use the six record labels for a two-minute check of how categories and training examples are chosen. I move directly to held-out evaluation and near-duplicate leakage if the learner can explain the distinction; we do not spend the block practising an obvious document sort.
I trace the training diagram in the deck: example, prediction, comparison and parameter update. I then supply a new example and name this inference.
I ask which data must stay unseen for evaluation and why near-duplicate agreements should not occur across both training and test.
In Terminal I run s02_vectors. I wait for completion and open the newly saved Embedding Selftest.txt, which reports the actual model and vector dimensions.
I read the vector shape and norms. I explain that the embedding coordinates are learned numerical representations; token IDs are names, not a meaningful distance scale.
Before reading each printed cosine pair, I ask which pair should be closer. I include the consent statement and its opposite, then inspect their actual similarity.
I say that high similarity can identify a related topic while missing a decisive negation. I do not turn a cosine into a legal interpretation.
I compare charge over property with charge for an offence. The learner names the context words. We return to the map and label its coordinates illustrative, separate from the measured self-test.
I ask for a two-sentence explanation to a partner: what changes in training, and what changes when a new file is uploaded. I record the explanation and any help needed.
check: The actual self-test produces normalized 384-dimensional vectors for this model; repeated text gives the same representation under this setup.
Opposite consent statements can be close. A similarity score is not a yes/no consent result.
Uploading context or indexing files does not by itself update model parameters. Provider retention/training use is a separate account-terms question.
discuss: A token has ID 900 and another has ID 901. Are they synonyms?
No. IDs identify units; closeness of identifiers is not semantic distance.
A training error curve falls. Is the model ready for our firm?
No. We need relevant held-out tests, leakage checks and consequences of errors.
rescue: Model download or import fails
I stop the live step and open the saved Neural Embedding self-test in the Mac Rehearsal evidence. I label it as saved measured output.
The learner treats the diagram as a real model visualization
I point to the illustrative label and separate it from the actual self-test values.
record: Run Record.json, Embedding Selftest.txt, the predicted versus observed pair comparison and one plain-language explanation in the progress record.
transition: I say: We can now distinguish learned patterns from the evidence supplied during a request; next we test what generated answers do with that evidence.
entry_question: A search model places two opposite consent sentences close together. Would you trust it to clear the transaction?
entry_focus: We use the measured vectors to explain related topic versus legal effect, then specify the held-out tests a vendor would need.
executive_task: Explain why a high similarity score cannot settle a consent exception. Then propose one evaluation case that similar training examples would not prepare the system to handle.
executive_check: The answer separates representation from legal interpretation and uses a genuinely held-out case, including an exception or negation. A falling training loss alone is insufficient.

title: How language models generate answers and fail
purpose: Test repeatability, source scope and missing information without staging a failure. Use the same matter and check every conclusion.
tool: Claude web for one fresh whole-agreement run and the source-scope/missing-fee tests; saved dated repeats for comparison; a text editor.
files: 03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/03 Research and Review/Generation Experiments.txt
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/03 Research and Review/Generation Run Record.csv
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/03 Research and Review/Evaluation Rubric.txt
04 Facilitator Materials/Teaching Resources/Checked Contract Answers.txt
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/01 Matter and Sources/Agreement - Executed v2.txt
04 Facilitator Materials/Teaching Resources/Demo Materials/Session 03 Standard Terms Only.txt
04 Facilitator Materials/Teaching Resources/Demo Materials/Session 03 Focused Consent Extract.txt
prepare: I prepare one fresh whole-agreement chat and the full agreement, Standard Terms-only file and focused extract as distinct attachments. I open the saved dated repeated runs before class. I do not use a persistent project containing the missing sources.

In Contract Retests I open R1 Prompt.txt and R1, R2 and R3 Response.txt; these three historical prompts are byte-identical. I label today’s whole-agreement answer F1, scope tests B1/B2 and missing-fee test C1.
steps: I run S03-P1 once in a fresh chat with the full agreement, label the answer F1 and record its model/date. We inspect the saved dated repeats with their own prompt. Today’s prompt differs, so F1 is not a controlled fourth repeat; we use the saved set to examine consistency.
I ask the learner to compare substance before style: trigger, exception, missing facts, source and conclusion. Three similar answers do not constitute independent source verification.
For B1 I start another fresh chat and attach only Session 03 Standard Terms Only.txt, then submit S03-P1. I do not reveal the missing Key Terms in that chat.
For B2 I use a fresh chat with only Session 03 Focused Consent Extract.txt and the same prompt. I compare its evidence scope with the full agreement, keeping unknown transaction facts unchanged.

I open the original Key Terms beside the Standard Terms-only answer. We identify what the restricted input could and could not establish; a source-scope difference is not a controlled product ranking.
For C1 I attach the full agreement in a fresh chat and submit S03-P2. I inspect the Order Form fee reference and confirm that the schedule itself is absent.
I choose one unsupported claim if a run contains one. I paste S03-P3 with that exact claim and location. I save the feedback-assisted revision separately from the initial response.
If every live answer is sound, I keep those successes. I then open a labelled failed historical run for the correction exercise, rather than changing inputs until failure appears.
I finish with the unrelated-buyer share-sale variant. We identify the change-of-control trigger and distinguish assignment voidness from general breach remedies in the checked key.

prompts.text: On the supplied evidence only, does Victoria’s consent apply to Equator’s proposed internal reorganisation? Transaction structure, ownership and continued responsibility are unconfirmed. Identify the applicable consent wording, exact supporting passage, established facts, missing facts and conditional conclusion. Do not assume an assignment or a change of control from the label alone. State any limits caused by omitted sources. Keep the answer within 250 words, excluding quoted source passages.

What are the annual Fees under this supplied executed agreement? Identify the exact source provision and whether the signed Fee Schedule itself has been supplied. Do not infer or invent a fee or a monetary liability cap. Distinguish a recital in the Order Form from independent inspection of the schedule.

Reviewer feedback: the following claim needs correction: [paste the actual unsupported sentence]. The source passage or missing evidence is: [paste the complete relevant wording or describe the gap]. Reassess the trigger, exception and conclusion using only established facts. Keep uncertainty explicit. Return a short revised draft and identify what changed. Do not alter the original response.

check: Historical repeats and today’s outputs are labelled separately. The saved set uses its recorded prompt and conditions; today uses S03-P1. Agreement does not validate an answer, and the two sets are not a controlled model comparison.
The Standard Terms-only run cannot establish the complete executed position without the override. The focused extract cannot establish every surrounding provision or transaction fact.
The correct missing-fee result requests the absent schedule. Feedback-assisted revisions are labelled as such; they do not become first-pass successes.
discuss: Why did a correctly quoted clause still produce a poor answer?
The model may have assumed a transaction fact or misapplied the exception.
What does a longer context window establish?
Capacity to supply more context; it does not guarantee faithful use.
rescue: Live requests exceed the allotted time
I retain the one live answer, compare the prepared dated evidence scopes, then prioritise the missing-fee and release-decision checks. I identify which outputs are live and which are saved.
The answer exceeds the requested length
I record that format failure separately from substantive correctness. I do not silently trim the saved raw output.
record: The source scope for every run, unchanged prompt and output, word-limit result, substantive checks, feedback and revised draft in separate files.
transition: I say: We have seen what can go wrong; next we practise giving a clear brief and checking the result.
entry_question: Several answers agree, and each quotes a real clause. What would make that agreement misleading?
entry_focus: We compare whole-agreement, Standard Terms-only and focused-extract evidence. We distinguish consistency, source completeness and correctness.
executive_task: Decide whether to release a coherent Standard-Terms-only answer that omits the overriding Key Terms. Identify the extra evidence needed.
executive_check: Hold release pending the governing version and transaction facts. Repeated generated answers cannot supply omitted evidence.

title: AI tools, effective instructions and safe use
purpose: Demonstrate a professional brief, source traceability, a review cycle and the questions needed before choosing a workplace tool.
tool: Claude web; one new chat per comparison; an existing account settings page and vendor due-diligence working copy.
files: 03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/03 Research and Review/Review Instruction.txt
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/01 Matter and Sources/Agreement - Executed v2.txt
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/01 Matter and Sources/Client Instruction.txt
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/01 Matter and Sources/Transaction Variants.txt
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/05 Firm Adoption/Vendor Due Diligence.csv
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/03 Research and Review/Evaluation Rubric.txt
prepare: I keep the evidence identical across the vague and structured runs. I open the same displayed model if the interface permits it, recording any difference.
I open the actual account settings without changing settings, adding connectors or entering employer data. I prepare a blank vendor record.
steps: I ask the learner to dictate the sort of brief they already use with AI, applied to this fictional agreement and instruction. I record it verbatim and run it in a fresh chat with those sources. I use S04-P1 only if a comparison baseline is needed; a vague prompt is not the primary lesson.

In a second fresh chat with the same files, I use S04-P2 as a review specification, adapting it only to the learner’s stated purpose and recording every change. We judge source support, missing facts and review effort rather than rewarding a more polished writing style.
I choose a material claim, open its quoted source and check whether the passage actually supports the claim. A source label alone is not the check.

The learner identifies one test the usual brief did not explicitly specify. I add it to a recorded revision and run the changed request if time permits. We check whether the result actually improves and keep a successful original answer as a success.
I introduce Variant A from the source file: an unrelated buyer acquires control. I paste S04-P3 into the relevant new comparison chat and test the changed conclusion.
On the account page, I record the actual account/product, data-use information shown, available controls and questions still unanswered. I do not infer workplace permission from a subscription price.
I compare the result with the rubric, then record one supported use, one exclusion and one procurement question for the firm.
I ask the learner to explain how a clear prompt and a human evidence check perform different jobs. I record the proposed reviewer and output boundary.

prompts.text: Review this contract and tell me whether the reorganisation can go ahead.

I advise Victoria, Customer in the attached fictional executed agreement. Review consent for Equator’s proposed internal reorganisation using only the agreement and instruction. Start with assignment and change-of-control triggers; both are unconfirmed. Read the Key Terms override. Return issue, source location, exact supporting passage, established facts, missing evidence and a conditional conclusion. Preserve exceptions and qualifications. Do not invent annual Fees or advise that a share sale is void under the assignment sentence. Label proposed changes separately. Produce a concise partner-review draft with no external action.

Change only this fact: an unrelated buyer acquires control of Equator through a share sale, with no assignment of the agreement stipulated. Reassess the relevant consent trigger and exception. Distinguish the assignment-voidness sentence from breach remedies. Identify unresolved legal and transaction questions and cite the supplied source. Keep this a review draft.

check: The structured brief makes evaluation easier but need not improve every answer. I accept a vague-prompt success if supported.
Variant A engages the stipulated change-of-control rule; it does not establish a transfer of the contract.
Retention, model training use, access, contractual permission and professional duties remain separate due-diligence entries.
discuss: What makes a citation useful?
The original passage exists, matches the version and supports the actual claim.
Does asking for certainty make an unknown fact known?
No. We request evidence or preserve uncertainty.
rescue: A cited location cannot be found
I hold the claim and ask for an exact passage, then search the original. If still absent, I mark it unsupported.
The account page omits a necessary term
I record it as an unanswered procurement question rather than invent a policy.
record: The learner’s usual brief verbatim, comparison specification, exact sources, raw outputs, review findings, changed-fact result and one reusable review or procurement decision.
transition: I say: A good brief still depends on good evidence; next we examine the firm’s information before a model receives it.
entry_question: How does your current way of briefing AI hold up when the source is incomplete or the transaction changes?
entry_focus: I start with the learner’s own usual brief on the fictional matter. We preserve what already works and test evidence, uncertainty and review effort.
executive_task: Turn the tested brief into a reusable review process. Decide what belongs in the instruction, what needs a maintained source collection and what must be checked by a reviewer.
executive_check: The process records source/version, acceptance tests and responsibility. A better prompt alone does not provide source maintenance, access enforcement or firm authority.

title: Preparing the firm’s information
purpose: Show how physical/scanned records become usable evidence and how extraction, structure, metadata and access can fail separately.
tool: Image viewer, Apple Vision OCR through the local launcher, text editor for JSON/XML and an inventory working copy.
files: 03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/02 Data and Retrieval/Original Source.png
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/02 Data and Retrieval/Synthetic Scan.png
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/02 Data and Retrieval/Degraded Scan - moderate.png
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/02 Data and Retrieval/Information Inventory.csv
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/02 Data and Retrieval/Document Quality Record.csv
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/02 Data and Retrieval/Clause Record.json
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/02 Data and Retrieval/Legal XML Teaching Fragment.xml
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/02 Data and Retrieval/Extraction Run Record.csv
prepare: I open the clean, mild and moderate images side by side, with the executed agreement available for verification. The degraded images are authored teaching approximations.
I run s05_ocr before class. I open the saved three Apple Vision OCR text outputs beside their corresponding images and keep both successes and omissions.
steps: I ask where information lives: paper rooms, scanned PDFs, Word/email, a document-management system such as NetDocuments, or a database. I record one generic system row without client identifiers.
For each row we name modality, structure and format separately: image, unstructured prose or a table, then PNG/PDF/DOCX/CSV. A searchable PDF can still have poor OCR.

I run s05_ocr live using Apple Vision fast/revision 2, CPU only, English and language correction off, or identify a saved engine/date. I compare the exact consent exception across each image and OCR output, including the words not required and continued responsibility.
I record any omission with source name, passage/location, observed extraction and required correction. I do not assume that every degraded image must fail on every engine.
I open Clause Record.json in a text editor and locate document_id, version, clause, text and source_location. I compare KT-1 with the original before trusting the structured record.

I open Legal XML Teaching Fragment.xml and show how marked sections can preserve a legal text’s structure. I explain that this is a teaching fragment, not certified Akoma Ntoso conversion of a whole legal collection.

We trace original, extraction, quality correction, structured representation, bounded passages, index and retrieved evidence. JSON, Markdown and legal XML are possible representations; converting to all three is not a compulsory pipeline.
I intentionally describe a metadata mistake: accurate M-01 words labelled OTHER-02. The learner explains how source identity and access can fail despite perfect OCR.
We assign a proposed source owner and a correction/re-indexing rule to the inventory row. I keep the original scan and any edited derivative separately.
check: The comparison is source-to-extraction, rather than a claim that the model understands a scanned contract.
The record preserves version, location and access context; a correct text string with the wrong matter tag is still unsuitable.
Chunking/indexing happen after source preparation, and an index is not the original authority.
discuss: What could reverse the legal meaning without changing most words?
Losing a negation or exception condition.
Must every file become legal XML?
No. Choose a usable representation that preserves the required structure, relationships and source traceability.
rescue: Local OCR cannot run
I open Observed OCR Output.txt beside the three source images and name its recorded Tesseract engine/date. I state that the live Apple Vision step did not run.
All three outputs are accurate
I keep the valid result, then inspect the separately labelled damaged extract or the recorded difficult condition. I do not claim a live failure occurred.
record: One inventory row, image-to-extraction comparison, quality/correction entry, metadata risk and proposed preparation gate.
transition: I say: Once the evidence is usable, the next question is how the system selects the right passages.
entry_question: The firm wants an internal assistant next month. Which collection is ready, and what would you stop from entering the index?
entry_focus: We trace a sample from its original system through extraction and metadata, identify a quality failure and define who clears it for use.
executive_task: Choose one collection such as scanned agreements or tax correspondence. Define its intake gate, correction owner and how a corrected source invalidates old derived content.
executive_check: The plan preserves original, provenance, version, access metadata and a correction/re-indexing route. Clean-looking text alone does not clear a collection.

title: Internal knowledge search and retrieval
purpose: Separate retrieval from generation and demonstrate the effects of source identity, input limits, ranking and amendment context.
tool: Local launcher with cached embedding models; the existing Google notebook for a source-grounded answer and citation inspection.

03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/02 Data and Retrieval/Knowledge Assistant Tests.csv
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/02 Data and Retrieval/Retrieval Scorecard.csv
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/02 Data and Retrieval/reviewed_retrieval.py
04 Facilitator Materials/Teaching Resources/Observed Runs/Corrections 2026-10-28/Token Limit Diagnosis.json
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/01 Matter and Sources/Agreement - Executed v2.txt
prepare: I run s06_baseline, s06_reviewed, s06_query and s06_missing before class. I open their saved text/JSON and identify hits versus mandatory_context.
I open the existing fictional retrieval notebook from the account route in the common setup. Only the executed agreement is selected. This is uploaded-document grounding, not an enterprise connector.
steps: I inspect the library manifest with the learner: 40 fictional sources, versions, matter tags, status and hashes. I choose CONTRACT-01 current obligations in M-01.
I run s06_baseline. I read the eight checks and the historical lexical failures K3 and K8. The launcher treats those as an expected baseline observation, not a repaired-route success.
I open Token Limit Diagnosis.json. The KT-1 passage had 728 tokens while the baseline encoder reads 256; its operative rule was outside the encoded portion.
I run s06_query and inspect the source ID/version, returned passages, source location and amendment context. I explain each added mechanism before comparing the result.

I run s06_reviewed. I distinguish the eight original questions from eleven added or strengthened safeguards. Identity and source purpose are explicit inputs, so this changed workflow is not an isolated model ranking.
I run s06_missing. The result must say no_source with no substitute hits. The learner explains why returning the familiar agreement would be a failure.
In the notebook I paste S06-P1. I click a material citation, read the source passage and compare its conclusion with the facts. I preserve a bad inference even if its citation is genuine.

If the notebook conflates assignment with the change-of-control exception, I paste S06-P2 and save the revision separately. I flag this as the teaching reading, with qualified interpretation if material.
The learner chooses a new question and source purpose. We identify what a representative firm test would add beyond the fixture, then write separate retrieval, answer and permission acceptance gates.

prompts.text: Use only the selected executed fictional agreement. Equator proposes an internal reorganisation; assignment, change of control, group ownership and continued responsibility are unconfirmed. Identify the two consent triggers separately and the Key Terms override. Quote the relevant passage and state which consent the exception follows. Keep the conclusion conditional. Also state whether the annual Fees can be established without the signed Fee Schedule. Cite the original source for each material claim; keep this a review draft.

Reviewer feedback: do not extend the group exception automatically to assignment consent. For this teaching reading, it follows and qualifies the change-of-control consent requirement. State the assignment rule and change-of-control rule separately, preserve both exception conditions and leave the current transaction facts unresolved. Flag any material interpretive ambiguity for qualified review. The triggers can coexist. Save this as a revised draft, not a first attempt.

check: The repaired suite reports 19/19 on the supplied fixture; the missing-source query returns no_source. Similarity scores remain evidence-ranking values.
The notebook keeps trigger uncertainty and the absent fee explicit. I check the inference as well as the quoted words.
Matter permissions in the local exercise are stipulated. No enterprise identity or cross-matter security certification is inferred.
discuss: A rule exists in the file; why might retrieval miss it?
It may be truncated, split without its context, filtered out or ranked below other passages.
All 19 checks pass. What should the firm test next?
Representative new matters, generated-answer fidelity and real access enforcement.
rescue: A model is not cached or a command fails
I use the correction evidence and diagnosis as saved output. I do not spend class time downloading models.
The notebook returns the correct source but an invented fact
I hold the answer, identify the unsupported inference and recheck a separately saved revision.
record: The four local run folders, selected source/purpose, actual retrieved IDs and context, one opened notebook citation, initial/revised answers and acceptance gates.
transition: I say: Internal evidence is one source problem; public legal research adds authority, time and conflicting sources.
entry_question: A relevant rule is in the library, yet the answer misses it. Is this a source, retrieval or reasoning failure?
entry_focus: We locate the actual failure in the trace, compare the repaired route and check the generated answer separately.
executive_task: Use the missing-source result to define when the assistant must ask for evidence. Add one representative firm test beyond the 19 fixture checks and explain which layer it tests.
executive_check: The proposed test distinguishes retrieval, answer fidelity and real access enforcement. Passing a small fixture does not certify a production system.

title: Legal research and deep research
purpose: Turn a research draft into a checked historical note by separating candidate sources, submissions, findings, arithmetic and current-law questions.
tool: Google notebook with only the original judgment selected; PDF viewer; independent arithmetic; a working Evidence Register.

03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/03 Research and Review/Research Brief.txt
03 Learner Materials/Practice Files/03 Research and Review/Evidence Register.csv

prepare: I open the public-law notebook and select only Goal Relief Judgment.pdf. I deselect the old generated report, secondary web pages and unrelated candidates, without deleting the historical evidence.
I open the original PDF at printed pages 1, 3 and 22–24. The local PDF has 24 pages; I verify whether viewer numbering and printed numbering match before citing.
steps: I state the scope: the High Court’s historical treatment of the programme delivery fee, not advice on Victoria’s current liability.
I ask the learner to predict the four assessment rows, the possible party/court confusion and the further sources a current opinion would require.
I paste S07-P1 into the notebook and wait for the complete answer. While it runs, we read page 1 and add only its four rows independently.
I compare the reported total with UGX 650,508,770. I keep the different figures appearing in grounds of appeal separate; adding them again would double-count descriptions.
I read pages 22–23 and mark what counsel submitted. I then read the court’s reasoning and the orders on pages 23–24. We identify the source role of each claim.
I click the appeal-rule and final-order citations in the answer. I compare the quoted text with printed page 3 and page 24, and record the exact location in the evidence register.

I check Act chapter and edition as the judgment cites them: Cap 341 for the appeal rule, Cap 338 for Income Tax and Cap 344 for VAT, in the 7th Revised Edition. Different current or earlier numbering is a separate verification task.

I flag the Tribunal-year discrepancy between the original High Court background and the official/listing sources. I identify the High Court by Civil Appeal 50 of 2023 and date; I do not silently choose a corrected year.

We draft three supported claims and a short historical note, then list current legislation, later treatment and client facts as unresolved research work. I compare with the checked note after the learner decides which claims survive.

prompts.text: Use only the selected original Goal Relief Judgment.pdf. Prepare a short historical verification note, not current legal advice. Transcribe the four assessment rows on printed page 1, preserving their labels, and add only those amounts. Keep amounts in grounds of appeal on pages 2–3 separate. Distinguish the appellant’s Ground 5 submissions on pages 22–23 from the court’s reasoning and orders on pages 23–24. Give the programme delivery fee holding and disposition with printed-page pinpoints. Report the Act chapters and editions exactly as cited on pages 3, 6, 10 and 22. Cite the original. Leave current applicability, later treatment and external metadata conflicts unresolved.

Discover primary public sources for Goal Relief Development Organisation v Uganda Revenue Authority, Civil Appeal 50 of 2023, High Court Commercial Division, 19 August 2024. Locate the original judgment, relevant historical legislation and any verifiable later appellate treatment. For each candidate state court or issuing body, date, exact URL, edition/period, access status and the proposition it might establish. Separate discovery from verification. Do not treat a search snippet, generated summary or absence of a result as clearance. Do not include client facts or produce current tax advice.

check: The court treated the fundraising/programme service as imported and held VAT correctly assessed; it affirmed the Tribunal, dismissed the appeal and awarded costs.
The historical note does not certify current legislation, later appellate treatment or Victoria’s position.
discuss: A genuine citation reproduces counsel’s submission. Can we call it the holding?
No. Identify the speaker and inspect the court’s actual reasoning and orders.
No later appeal appears in a limited search. What can we say?
Only what was searched, when, and what was verified; not that no later authority exists.
rescue: The web original is blocked
I inspect the saved original PDF and mark fresh source discovery incomplete. I do not replace authority with an unverified summary.
The report is polished but fails arithmetic or pinpoints
I hold the affected claims, correct them against the original and preserve the failed output.
record: The selected source, exact prompt/answer, four-row arithmetic, three claim records with source role/page, opened citations and unresolved current-law questions.
transition: I say: We will now apply the same discipline to reviewing and drafting contractual language.
optional: Before class or in agreed extra time, choose Deep Research in the source-search box, paste S07-P2 and review the plan. Inspect sources before importing; completion is not verification.
entry_question: A polished research note has genuine citations. Which claims could go into advice today?
entry_focus: We audit source role, historical edition, arithmetic and page location, then separate verified historical claims from current-law work still required.
executive_task: A colleague wants to reuse the historical tax note in a current matter. Which legislation, later-treatment checks and client facts are still required?
executive_check: Assign each material claim to an authority and period. Name the unresolved checks; a generated report or empty search result cannot clear current advice.

I attach the playbook, client instruction and flawed review, then paste S08-P2. I retain the output as a proposed review table.

I read Variant B aloud: an assignment to another company is proposed. I ask for the first assignment sentence before considering the separate change-of-control exception. I preserve facts not supplied about the assignee.

For the unrelated-buyer share-sale question, we distinguish the assignment-voidness sentence and follow Sections 5.3(a), 5.3(b)(i), 8.1–8.4, the Key Terms and 12.5 before describing possible remedies.
I paste S08-P3. We compare the proposed amendment with the agreed text, checking actor, permission, condition, exception and unintended effect.

prompts.text: Extract the named parties, organisations, dates and monetary references from the supplied fictional agreement. For each give the exact source span, location and tentative entity type. Separately identify the contractual role and the surrounding wording supporting it. Do not infer an obligation or a missing fee from the name alone. Mark uncertain roles and distinguish Order Form recitals from independently verified facts.

Review the attached constructed Flawed Contract Review against the full executed agreement, client instruction and customer-side playbook. Return issue, source version/location, exact supporting passage, missing facts, qualification and proposed correction. Start with the transaction trigger before exceptions. Read KT-1 and KT-2. Do not invent a fee or conflate share sale with assignment. Follow relevant remedy cross-references rather than claiming no consequences exist. Keep agreed obligations separate from proposals and legal questions needing qualified review.

Draft one customer-side amendment addressing the specific issue we selected: [state the actual selected issue]. Show the current wording beside the proposed wording, explain the commercial reason and identify any changed actor, consent condition, exception or remedy. Use no invented fee. Mark the wording as a proposal requiring partner review and negotiation. Do not claim that the proposed text is already agreed.

check: The replaced first sentence requires assignment consent; under the teaching reading the following group exception qualifies change-of-control consent, with interpretive review if material.
KT-2 requires each support person to be named in a written request and approved in writing before access. The annual fee remains unestablished without the schedule.
A possible breach remedy retains materiality, cure, liability qualifications and source limits; a share sale is not automatically void under the assignment sentence.
discuss: The model found a company name. Has it found the obligation?
No. We need the actor, operative wording, conditions and surrounding context.
An amendment sounds commercially reasonable. Can it be treated as the current contract?
No. Label the proposal and obtain review/negotiation.
rescue: The review uses only the original Standard Terms

A draft invents an assignee, fee or automatic termination

record: Entity-versus-role example, checked review rows, current/proposed amendment comparison, reason, source locations and proposed reviewer.
transition: I say: Drafting is one output; next we decide what happens when a system can choose or execute a step.
entry_question: A review identifies the parties correctly. Has it established their obligations, and is the proposed amendment acceptable?
entry_focus: We follow entities into operative provisions and cross-references, then inspect one amendment for changed rights, conditions and unintended effects.
executive_task: Choose one review finding and negotiate the proposed clause change aloud. What commercial protection improves, and what new ambiguity or burden could the amendment create?
executive_check: The explanation compares current and proposed text, preserves unknown facts, checks cross-references and separates a proposal from agreed obligations.

prompts.text: Use only the fictional CONTRACT-01 v2 clause supplied below. Equator proposes an internal reorganisation; assignment, change of control, ownership and continued responsibility are unconfirmed. Separate the two consent triggers; do not infer either from the label. Under the teaching reading the group exception follows change-of-control consent. Preserve both conditions and flag material interpretation for review. Return four plain-text fields: consent_summary, source_quote, open_facts, review_status. Keep the conclusion unresolved until facts establish it. Take no external action. CLAUSE: CONTRACT-01 v2 KT-1 | Neither party may assign any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other party. In addition, Provider must obtain Customer’s prior written consent before a change of control of Provider takes effect. That consent is not required for a reorganization within a wholly owned group if Provider remains responsible for its obligations under this Agreement. Any attempted but non-permitted assignment is void. This Agreement will be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties and their permitted successors and assigns.

check: The actual trace shows model-selected lookup and host execution. The answer must also preserve trigger uncertainty and source qualifications.
The host suite passes seven tests and the protocol suite three. A malformed response is held rather than repaired into an executable request.
The local page holds changed fields, declined approval and an unapproved recipient. It is deterministic and has no URA or external-action connection.

The execution host enforces permitted tools and arguments; a prompt alone is insufficient.
Can correct access produce an incorrect answer?
Yes. We inspect the draft’s facts and inference after the safe lookup.

The model returns malformed JSON

Zapier asks for an upgrade or a new connection
I use the existing saved full-test evidence and proceed to the local agent. Class time does not depend on a purchase or provisioning.

At minute 0 of the 35-minute incident block, I read Incident Exercise.txt: OTHER-02 content appeared in an M-01 user’s draft. I ask for the first containment action before supplying the next detail.
Minutes 0–8: we stop the affected retrieval/output route and hold the draft. I preserve the query, access context, source identifiers, output and recipients without reproducing restricted text.

Minutes 8–18: we identify who saw or received the passage, which permissions were involved and the firm roles that must assess professional, contractual and data duties. I do not invent a universal reporting deadline.
Minutes 18–28: the learner proposes cause investigation, access correction, derived-index checks and an adversarial retest. I ask how we would know the correction worked.

Minutes 28–35: we define an authorised restart decision, evidence needed and a communication owner. I change the scenario from a retrieved paragraph to an attached email and ask which controls change.
We adapt one approved-use rule with permitted evidence, excluded actions, reviewer, reporting route and review date. These are proposed firm decisions for later approval.
check: Each risk has an owner and a testable control. No-training, retention, access and professional permission are assessed separately.
The first incident action contains exposure and preserves evidence. Restart requires verified correction and an authorised decision.
The OCR evidence supports a document-condition quality discussion; claims about protected groups need representative data and separate analysis.
discuss: A vendor says no-training. What remains to check?
Retention, access, contracts, location, recipients, purpose and professional permission.
Who can authorise restart?
The firm’s designated responsible authority after the agreed tests and legal/professional assessment, rather than the AI tool itself.
rescue: The learner proposes only a policy slogan
I ask who performs the control, where it is enforced and what evidence would show it failed.
A precise legal deadline is requested
I identify the relevant legal question and source to verify; I do not turn the classroom source map into current advice.
record: One revised risk row, the incident decision log, source-quality observation, proposed rule and explicit restart conditions.
transition: I say: We can now decide what a first organisational pilot should cost, prove and stop for.
entry_question: An assistant puts another matter’s restricted material into a draft. What happens in the first few minutes?
entry_focus: We rehearse containment, evidence preservation, affected recipients and restart authority. Each proposed control needs an owner and a failure test.
executive_task: Draft a usable rule for this incident route, then explain how the firm will know the rule is followed. Identify who can authorise restart and what evidence they need.
executive_check: The rule specifies a permitted purpose, responsible roles, enforceable controls, tests and a reporting route. A policy statement without operational evidence is incomplete.

I ask the learner to predict whether the main and stress cases justify proceeding. I calculate manually with a calculator or formulas, then run s12_costs as an independent check.

We compare main review cost 800,000 with manual 1,200,000 and tool costs 240,000: a 160,000 monthly capacity-value difference. The stress case gives negative 360,000. These are fictional planning assumptions, not vendor quotes or guaranteed cash savings.

I present a counterexample: the draft saves time but omits a critical exception. The learner decides stop/revise rather than expand on speed alone.

Only if the capacity produces an evidenced avoidable cost or revenue effect.
The demo works once. Expand to the entire firm?
